entries.title: The Currently log
entries.summary: Every change of Petto is posted in this channel when it goes live: a color for each kind of change, a short explanation, and pictures. React with the like or the dislike to tell us what you think. Red is security, yellow a new feature, green something added to a feature, blue an improvement, orange a fix, purple the web and docs, gray something removed and black a feature removed.

entries.title: Top lists of the best partner managers
entries.summary: `{partner.top_list_day}`, `{partner.top_list_week}` and `{partner.top_list_total}` write the five best managers of the day, the week and all time, one per line with their partnerships. Use them in any partner message.

entries.title: 14 new server and member variables
entries.summary: Server: `{server_age_days}`, `{server_createdate_timestamp}`, `{server_emojicount}`, `{server_stickercount}`, `{server_description}`, `{server_vanity}`, `{server_banner}`, `{server_verification}`, `{server_locale}` and `{server_rules_channel}`. Member: `{user.role_count}`, `{user.top_role_mention}`, `{user.is_owner}` and `{user.joined_age_days}`.

entries.title: Purge in every channel
entries.summary: `/purge` and `!purge` have a new option, `all_channels` (or `!purge everywhere 50 bots`). It scans every text channel where you and Petto can delete, shows how many messages it would delete in each one, and waits for a Confirm click before deleting anything.

entries.title: New command: /mhistory
entries.summary: `/mhistory moderator:<member>` and `!mhistory <moderator>` show the cases a moderator has given. The line of `/case stats` that pointed to it now names a command that exists.

entries.title: A case shows the same icon everywhere
entries.summary: The card of a case (`/case view`, `/case edit`) and the one-line case still used the old icon of each sanction type. They now use the hammer, or the alert for a warning, like the list of cases.

entries.title: /forum outside a post says why
entries.summary: Using `/forum` in a channel that is not a forum post answered with a generic error. It now tells you to use it inside a post.

entries.title: /guildtag and /vanity show in the menu
entries.summary: Discord hid both commands from members without Manage Server, so a moderator could not find them. They now show for everybody and ask for Manage Server when they run.

entries.title: !c opens the cases
entries.summary: `!c <member>` is now a short way of `!case`: it shows the cases of that member.

entries.title: !c is no longer the calculator
entries.summary: `c` was a short word of the calculator, so `!c <id>` answered with a calculation. `!calc` and `!calculate` still work.

entries.title: New blog post: Introducing the Currently log
entries.summary: What the Currently log is, what each color means, how a post looks and what is in the first one. Available in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: A sticky message is posted when you save it
entries.summary: Saving a sticky message in the dashboard now posts it in the channel right away, like `!stickymessage set` does, instead of waiting for somebody to write there first. If you change it, the old message is replaced.

entries.title: Text fields fit their text
entries.summary: Every text field of the site has the height of its text: no corner to drag, it grows as you write and shrinks as you delete, and an empty one is four lines high. Chat boxes keep their own size.

entries.title: The "New" label goes away by itself
entries.summary: The "New" label on the tabs of the dashboard, the modules, the menu and the footer now lasts ten days from the day something comes out. The ones that were still showing it after weeks are gone.

entries.title: Sticky messages come back down for bots too
entries.summary: A sticky message used to ignore what bots wrote, so in a channel where bots do the talking it stayed far above. Now a message from anybody (members, bots and webhooks) brings it back to the bottom.

entries.title: A ban with deleted messages answers first
entries.summary: When you ban someone and ask to delete their recent messages, Petto now sends the notice, bans, says it is done and writes the log first, and deletes the messages after. Before, a member with many messages made you wait for the deletion before seeing the answer.

entries.title: Purge in every channel also cleans threads and forum posts
entries.summary: `/purge all_channels` skipped threads and the posts of forums, so what was written there stayed. It now scans the open ones too, and they appear in the confirmation list. An archived thread is left alone: nothing can be deleted there until it is opened again.

entries.title: Ticket transcripts show forwarded messages
entries.summary: A forwarded message used to appear in the transcript as "No text content", because the text lives in the original message. Now the transcript shows what was forwarded (its text, embeds, files and stickers) under a "Forwarded" mark, and the live view of the ticket shows it too.

entries.title: Petto Code can now manage the server
entries.summary: Commands written in code can now edit, delete and pin messages, read messages, users and permissions, and run a command later. From a button, a menu, a form or a reaction they can also moderate (warn, mute, kick, ban), lock channels and manage roles, threads and nicknames, always with the permissions of the member who pressed it: a typed command cannot copy what Petto already does with its own commands. There are also 30 small tools for text, numbers, lists and dates.

entries.title: Petto Code: files, connected commands and reminders that repeat
entries.summary: A command can now be written in several files: the + above the editor adds one (up to 5), and they run together as one code. A command can use another one (callCC) and give a value back, run a command of Petto as the member (runCommand), and run by itself every some time, every day or every week in a time zone. One panel under the editor sets what starts it, the commands that run after it, who can use it and where (roles and channels), what a mistake does, and the server time zone. The editor is also bigger on a phone.

entries.title: Roles and channels are easier to pick in the dashboard
entries.area: Dashboard › Lists of roles and channels
entries.summary: Every list of roles and channels in the dashboard now has a box to tick in each row. Roles show their color, channels sit under their category like in Discord, and a role that Petto cannot give (above Petto, or managed) shows dark and locked with the reason. A list that only filters keeps those roles, with a small mark. On a phone the same compact menu opens, and tapping a text field closes an open list, so what you type goes to that field.

entries.title: Roles in their own color, categories with their emoji
entries.area: Dashboard › Lists of roles and channels
entries.summary: In every list of the dashboard a role is now written in its own color, as Discord shows it, and in the chip that stays when it is chosen. A category whose name starts with an emoji shows that emoji first in its title, in the lists and in the compact menu. Tapping a text field while a list is open now puts the phone's keyboard in that field, never in the list, and the file tabs of the code editor meet the code box with one soft outline.

entries.title: One Save button for the whole Code page
entries.summary: Change the options of a command, the time zone, the connected commands, the trigger or the code, and the bar at the bottom says "You have unsaved changes" with Discard and Save changes for all of it together. Save sends every change, one after the other; Discard puts everything back as it was.

entries.title: A little ring turns inside a switch while it saves
entries.summary: Every switch of the dashboard is the same green, and while a change is being saved a small ring turns inside its knob, like the ones of the quick access in the overview. The page does not reload, so it feels smoother.

entries.title: Green to save and choose, red to delete
entries.summary: In the dashboard, the buttons that save or add are green, the ones that delete are red, and what you have chosen (options, chips, tabs and ticks) is green too. The peach stays for the menu and the links.

entries.title: The log of a sanction that ends shows who it was
entries.summary: When a timed mute or ban ends by itself, the log now shows the name, the ID and the avatar of the person at the top, like the log of a new sanction. Before, it only had the ID.

entries.title: `!level roles` shows the roles of the levels
entries.summary: `!level roles` (and `!level rewards`) is the same as `!level reward list` and `/level reward list`: the roles you get at each level. Before, it said it could not find `roles`.

entries.title: The color card says why it has no picture
entries.summary: `/search color`, `!color` and `!hex` draw a picture of the color. Where Petto or the member cannot attach files in the channel, the picture was left out without a word; now the card says why, so you know to give Petto the Attach Files permission.

entries.title: A bulk role job no longer stops with an error when the server is just back
entries.summary: If the roles of the server were not loaded yet (the server had just come back, or Discord was slow), a bulk role job stopped with an unexpected error. Now Petto loads the roles first, and if it still cannot read them it says so and you can start the job again.

entries.title: Petto's libraries are up to date
entries.summary: Four of the libraries Petto uses were updated to their latest versions (images, settings, the request limit and the payments kit). Nothing changes for you, but it keeps Petto safe and ready for what comes.

entries.title: The Petto Code wiki has a step by step guide, recipes and a full reference
entries.summary: The Petto Code wiki is much longer: a guide that goes step by step, ten recipes you can copy (a welcome, a shop, a reminder...), and a reference of every function with an example. On a phone, the tables are cards, so a long name is never cut in the middle.

entries.title: Tables of the wiki are cards on a phone
entries.summary: On a phone, each row of a table of the wiki (like the variables) is a card, so a long variable is never cut in the middle and you do not have to scroll sideways.

entries.title: The Code Generator knows every function of Petto Code
entries.summary: The Code Generator (version 1.7.0) runs the same engine as the bot again: all the new functions of Petto Code, connected commands, repeating reminders, and the mistakes it finds are written in the language of the page.

entries.title: A change reaches the Currently log in two minutes
entries.summary: Petto now looks for new changes every two minutes, not every ten, so what is merged and deployed shows in this channel almost at once instead of looking like it was forgotten.

entries.title: The pictures of a change are checked before it is posted
entries.summary: Petto now reads each picture of a change the way Discord does (it has to be a real image of a size Discord takes) and leaves it ready, so one of the three pictures of a change no longer shows broken. A change whose picture does not pass waits until it does.

entries.title: The Improvements card has an arrow that goes up
entries.summary: The card of the improvements had two circular arrows that looked like a clock. It now has an arrow that goes up.

entries.title: Petto uses less memory
entries.summary: Petto used a lot of memory keeping every message it saw for an hour, even in servers that do not use the message log. Now it keeps them for ten minutes, and for an hour only in the servers that have the message log on, so the log of edited and deleted messages works as before. A lighter Petto stays fast as it grows.

entries.title: The statistics overview shows voice next to messages
entries.summary: The overview of the statistics now draws the voice hours per day and the busiest hours of voice right next to the messages per day and the busiest hours of messages, so you see both at a glance. The Voice tab keeps its own details.

entries.title: Petto no longer works for logs a server did not turn on
entries.summary: Before building a log, Petto now checks that the server has that log on. A server without the voice log or the message log no longer makes Petto ask Discord who muted, moved or disconnected someone, or build the embed for every edit and deletion. Servers with the logs on get them exactly as before.

entries.title: /stats member now comes as two picture cards
entries.summary: /stats member shows a profile card with the member's server rank for messages and voice, when the account was created and when they joined, and their messages and voice time in the last day, 7 days and 30 days. Under it, a second card has the streak, active days, best day and a chart of messages and voice hours per day. Voice time counts now, not only messages. Every /stats picture now shows the icon of your server next to its name. The pictures here show the main Petto server with made-up numbers.

entries.title: A channel Petto cannot see is no longer called deleted
entries.summary: Discord now shows the channels a bot cannot view only in outline. The dashboard used to call a saved choice that pointed to one of them (a log, a feed, a honeypot or a paginated list) a deleted channel. It now says No access (hidden channel), because the channel exists and Petto just cannot see it. The channel pickers still do not list those channels.

entries.title: Tickets answered by AI are removed
entries.summary: The AI assistant for tickets is gone, for good. Its answers were not reliable enough and it used more resources than it was worth. Petto no longer greets or answers in new tickets with the AI, the Talk to a person button and the AI assistant page of the dashboard are removed, and so are its settings in the server's YAML. Staff answer tickets as always. The /ask command stays.

entries.title: Privacy Policy and Terms explain /ask and follow Canadian law
entries.summary: The Privacy Policy and the Terms now explain how /ask works: only the question, and up to four earlier messages of a conversation, go to the AI provider; Petto stores none of it and does not use it to train AI; the provider may process it outside Canada. Petto follows the principles of Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA, and Law 25 in Québec) and names Liam as the person responsible for privacy. The Terms are governed by the laws of Colombia. The old texts about the ticket assistant are gone.

entries.title: /language and /support are slash commands
entries.summary: /language, to see or change the language Petto speaks on your server, and the new /support, which gives you the invitation to the support server, now work as slash commands. The prefix commands !language and !support keep working too.

entries.title: The welcome message of a new server uses slash commands
entries.summary: When Petto joins a server, the setup message and the guide for the owner now point to /help, /logs, /automod, /greet and /language instead of the prefix commands, and the invitation to the support server is in it. The picture next to the text is the avatar Petto has in that server, so a Christmas avatar shows up too, and every line has its icon.

entries.title: The dashboard login asks if you want to join the support server
entries.summary: The first time you sign in to the dashboard, a question asks whether you want Petto to add you to the support server, with Yes and No. Only if you say yes does Discord ask you to allow it on its own screen. It is asked once, and nobody is added without saying yes.

entries.title: The wiki publishes again and the Priority changelog is up to date
entries.summary: The wiki had stopped publishing its latest changes because of an error in a file meant for the team. It is fixed, so what was written about /ask and privacy is online. The Priority changelog now shows the news of 2026-11-18 and its text no longer sits in a narrow column under the date. The Language and Statistics pages describe /language and the new /stats member pictures.

entries.title: What Petto stored for a server is deleted 5 minutes after it is removed
entries.summary: When Petto is removed from a server, everything it stored for that server is deleted at most 5 minutes later, not after 3 days: the settings, the logs and the backups kept in its database, with no exceptions (a Premium slot in use or backups no longer make it wait). If the bot is added back inside those minutes, nothing is lost. The servers that were waiting for their 3 days are deleted now. The Privacy Policy says so in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: Quick Setup: set up your server in seven steps from the dashboard
entries.summary: A new guided setup in the dashboard menu. Pick the modules you want (moderation log, auto moderation, welcome messages, auto role, tickets, verification), answer a few questions in each step and nothing changes in your server until the last step, when everything is applied together. Petto can make the channels and roles for you, and a step that fails does not stop the others. You can run it again any time from the sidebar.

entries.title: Moderation rules: make your own rules in the dashboard
entries.summary: A new, much more powerful way to moderate. Make rulesets with general conditions (channels, categories, roles, new accounts) and rules inside them: choose what to look for (words, links with allow and deny lists, invites, mentions, caps, emojis, repeated or too fast messages, attachments and more), who and where it applies, and what Petto does (delete, reply, DM, warn, timeout, kick, ban, give or take a role), even only after a member does it several times. There is a log of what each rule did, without the text of messages. Rules are made only in the dashboard.

entries.title: Every page of the dashboard now ends with what happens to your data
entries.summary: At the bottom of every server page there is now a short note: Petto keeps your settings while it is in your server, deletes them within 5 minutes if you remove it, and where to make a backup, export your settings, read the docs, get support or read the Privacy Policy.

entries.title: Moderation rules: strikes, heat, join gate, rule tester and more
entries.summary: Moderation rules grow. Strikes and heat: count what a member does (kept in the database, so a restart forgets nothing), and let timeouts grow each time. New triggers (busy channel, fast mentions, files or links, names, strikes, heat), conditions (bot or person, edited message, threads) and effects (delete their last messages, slowmode, alert, quarantine, lock the server). A test mode, a Try this rule panel, ready-made templates, and export and import. A join gate for avatars, new accounts and names, with a raid detector. Big lists are searched much faster.

entries.title: Dashboard: modules on or off in the menu, clearer Overview and pictures in the Audit Log
entries.area: Dashboard › Menu, Overview and Audit Log
entries.summary: The dashboard looks and moves better. The side menu now shows what is on: a green dot for a module that is on and grey for the ones that are off, and a section is grey when none of its modules is on. New things carry a NEW label again (not a bare dot). The Overview cards are clearer, with a mark on the edge, a dot for the state and a button to the settings that fits a phone. Colors keep their mark (border, dot, icon) but the words stay light and easy to read. The Audit Log shows the picture of who did each change.

entries.title: Dashboard: a Welcome section, a Roles section and a menu that makes sense
entries.summary: The old Join Gate page that mixed everything is split. Welcome is now its own section: welcome messages, DM on join and ping on join. Verification stays in Security. Bump goes to Community. Roles is a new section that gathers join roles, aged roles, reaction roles, sticky roles, bulk roles, role triggers, role quotas, booster roles and vanity roles. Old links and bookmarks send you to the new pages by themselves.

entries.title: Up to 25 welcome, goodbye and boost messages: Petto picks one at random
entries.summary: Like other bots do: instead of one sentence for everybody, a server can have up to 25 messages for the welcome, 25 for the goodbye and 25 for the boost. Each time, Petto picks one at random and never the same one twice in a row. Add them with the button "Add another message" in the dashboard, or with /greet welcome add-message (also for leave and boost). Each one can be a text or a saved embed.

entries.title: Aged roles: a role after some days in the server
entries.summary: Give a role to whoever has been in the server for some days, and take another one away at the same time (for example after 30 days give Regular and take New). Make as many rules as you need (up to 25), for humans, bots or everybody. Petto looks about every 30 minutes, and the members who were already in get it too. Add rules in the dashboard (Roles › Aged roles) or with /role aged add.

entries.title: Staff roles: let a role ban or mute without the Discord permission
entries.summary: A Mod role that can ban without having Ban Members, a helper role that can only warn: for each moderation action (ban, kick, mute, warn, unban, cases, notes and more) you choose which roles may use it. It was already possible with /moderation allow; now you can see and change everything in one page of the dashboard. Only who manages the server can open it. Bulk actions stay for administrators.

entries.title: Quests and Rollouts are now one section in the menu
entries.summary: The Quest alerts and Rollout alerts pages were each in a section of their own with a single page inside. They now share one section, Quests and Rollouts, so the menu is shorter. Nothing else changes: each page is the same and is shown only to the people who could already open it.

entries.title: /levels manage no longer fails with a huge level or XP
entries.summary: Setting a level like 20 billion with /levels manage made a number too big for the database and the command failed with an error. Now Petto tells you the highest level of your server (or the most XP one member can have) and saves nothing, so nobody's level is changed by a typo. Normal changes work as before.

entries.title: New blog guides: Petto compared with other bots, and how to switch from MEE6, Carl-bot or Dyno
entries.summary: Four new posts, in English, Spanish and Portuguese. One puts Petto next to MEE6, Carl-bot and Dyno using what their own pages say (checked on November 18, 2026): what is free, what is paid and where Petto is behind, such as the economy it does not have. The other three are step-by-step guides to leave MEE6, Carl-bot or Dyno without a gap, with a table of where each feature lives in Petto, what does not move, and pictures of the dashboard and of Discord. The home page now pins the comparison instead of the Kobot announcement.

entries.title: The footer now says © 2017–2026 and all rights reserved
entries.summary: Petto did not start in 2026: the bot has been around since 2017. The footer of the website now says © 2017–2026, all rights reserved, and that Petto is not affiliated with Discord, in English, Spanish and Portuguese. The line at the top of the home page says Discord bot · since 2017 instead of actively developed. The covers of the new blog guides now show the icon of each bot and the default 3D avatar of Petto, with no names.

entries.title: New page "Migrate from another bot": convert your messages and follow a checklist
entries.summary: Moving from MEE6, Carl-bot or Dyno is easier now. Paste a welcome or any message written for the old bot and Petto rewrites its variables into Petto's, shows what changed, what has no equivalent and why, and how it will read. Below there is a checklist of what to rebuild, with a button to open the page of Petto where each thing lives; your ticks stay in your browser. A bot cannot read the settings of another one, so nothing is imported by itself. ProBot and Welcomer are listed but their variables are not checked yet, so Petto does not guess.

entries.title: The Migrate page has an AI helper: rewrite, plan and ask
entries.summary: Tags, commands and autoresponders of another bot are more than a list of variables, so the Migrate page now has an AI helper. Paste something from the old bot and it rewrites it for Petto; describe what you had and it proposes what to set up and where; or ask a question about moving. It only proposes: it never changes your server, you copy what you want. Petto checks the variables it writes and warns about any that do not exist. Only people with Manage Server can use it, there is a wait between questions, and your text is not stored.

entries.title: The wiki guide for moving from another bot explains the Migrate page
entries.summary: The guide Migrating From Another Bot now has a section about the new Migrate page of the dashboard, in English, Spanish and Portuguese: how the converter rewrites the variables of MEE6, Carl-bot and Dyno (with a table of the most used ones and what has no equivalent), how the checklist works, and what the AI helper does, who can use it and what happens to your text. The changelog of the wiki has it too.

entries.title: The comparison table of the blog is easier to read on a phone
entries.summary: In the post that compares Petto with MEE6, Carl-bot and Dyno, the five-column table made you scroll sideways and covered the text. On a phone each row is now a card: the name of the thing on top and one line for each bot below it. On a computer the table looks the same as before.

entries.title: The answer of the AI helper shows bold, code and lists instead of asterisks
entries.summary: The AI helper of the Migrate page wrote its answers with markdown, and the page showed the marks as they were: **words** with asterisks and `code` with loose quotes. Now the answer is drawn with its format: bold, italics, code, titles and numbered or bulleted lists, and the parts for Petto stay in their own block with a Copy button. Nothing the AI writes can become code of the page: it is only ever shown as text.

entries.title: The Migrate page now converts ProBot and Nekotina messages
entries.summary: ProBot and Nekotina join MEE6, Carl-bot and Dyno on the Migrate page. Paste a ProBot message ([user], [server], [memberCount]...) or a Nekotina one ({{user}}, {{server}}, {{members}}...) and Petto rewrites it with its own variables, and each bot has its own checklist with a button to the page of Petto for every thing it did. The variables are the ones in their official guides (docs.probot.io and nekotina.com). Welcomer still has no list: its website does not let its documentation be read, so Petto does not guess and gives your text back as you wrote it.

entries.title: The team can delete comments on the feedback board
entries.summary: Until now the team could delete a post of the feedback board but not a comment. Now every comment has a delete button for the team, with a question first ("Delete this comment? This cannot be undone."). The comment count of the post and its card in Discord are updated. Only the team sees the button; members cannot delete other people's comments.

entries.title: Petto now says exactly which permission is missing
entries.summary: When something fails because Petto lacks a permission, it no longer says only "I am missing a permission". It reads the error, looks at what it really has and tells you: for example "I am missing Ban Members in this server" or "I am missing Send Messages in #welcome". If the problem is a role (it is above Petto's, or it belongs to an integration) or a member who is above Petto, it says that instead. When it cannot know, it keeps the old generic text. Works in commands, buttons and tickets.

entries.title: Permission problems reach the staff: log channel and Overview
entries.summary: When something Petto tried to do fails because of a permission, the staff now hears about it. The notice goes to the private log channel of the server (never to the owner's DMs) and says what failed, which permission is missing and where. The same problem is told once a day at most, however many times it happens. The Overview of the dashboard shows a card with every active problem, a "Check again" button and a dismiss button; what you fix goes away by itself. Only people with Manage Server see it.

entries.title: Quick Setup could not turn on the audit logs
entries.summary: The "Audit logs" step of the setup failed in some servers because the database did not accept the new forum log category. It is accepted now, so the setup can route every kind of log to your log channel, and the forum log can be chosen again.

entries.title: Official AutoMod rules: no more failures after the fifth rule
entries.summary: Discord only lets one person create 5 AutoMod rules every 30 seconds. When Petto made all its rules at once, the ones after the fifth failed and stayed missing. Now Petto waits the time Discord says and tries again, so all the rules get created (it can take about half a minute).

entries.title: Reddit feeds are no longer switched off as "the account does not exist"
entries.summary: Reddit sometimes answers "Not Found" to a request it does not like, even for subreddits that exist, and Petto believed it and switched the feed off. Now a "not found" from the feed address is only believed when Reddit's second way of reading (JSON) says it too; if not, the feed counts as blocked or unavailable and is tried again, never turned off for a missing account. A feed that was already switched off can be resumed in Feeds.

entries.title: Notices for the staff no longer go to the owner's DMs
entries.summary: When something needed the staff's attention (a feed switched off, a verification role that could not be given, a permission problem), Petto sent the notice to the owner by direct message if the server had no private log channel. That filled the owner's DMs with messages nobody asked for. Now these notices go only to the private log channel of the server. If there is none, nothing is sent by DM; permission problems are always in the Overview of the dashboard.

entries.title: The menu and the language button of the top bar open on any phone, even in the login page
entries.summary: On some phones the burger menu and the language button did nothing, for example in the page that says Login required. Both depended on the big script of the page: if a browser was too old for it, a blocker stopped it or it loaded late, nothing opened. They now run from a small separate script written in plain old JavaScript, placed right after the menu, so they open even if the rest of the page script fails. It was tested by blocking every script file of the page: before, the menu did not open; now it does.

entries.title: Migrate from another bot is now marked as Beta
entries.summary: The page is not finished: more variables and more help from the AI (to set things up for you) are still to come. So the menu and the page now say Beta instead of New, with a short note. The copy buttons of the page also have the look of the rest of the dashboard now (before they were the grey ones of the public site).

entries.title: Message roles: a role when a member reaches a number of messages
entries.summary: New Message roles page (Roles → Message roles) and /messagerole command. Pick a role and a number: when a member reaches it, Petto gives the role right after that message. Count all the messages since you add the first rule, or only the ones of the last days, and choose to take the role away if the member falls under the number. Up to 25 rules, each with its own switch. Petto counts from the moment the first rule is added; bots never count.

entries.title: Quest alerts now come with their limits and pictures
entries.summary: A new quest is announced only when the main quest list has it, so the alert already shows the countries, the age limit, the decoration and the Orbs picture from the first message. Before, the first alert could come from a list that does not know the limits, and they only showed later in /quests. The other lists still fill in blanks and keep /quests complete, and if the main list has no new quest for 7 days they announce too, until it has one again.

entries.title: Block a member from XP
entries.summary: You can now block a member from XP: they earn none by chatting or in voice, and nobody can give them any by hand with /levels manage xp or level. Their XP stays as it is, and /levels manage block lists who is blocked. Use /levels manage block member:@someone to block or let out, or the new Members blocked from XP box in the Rules page of Leveling (up to 100 members).

entries.title: A darker web, a calmer dashboard with fewer colors, and a shorter footer
entries.summary: The whole website is now dark with the footer in the same tone (the dashboard is a little darker, near black). The dashboard uses a short palette (peach, green, red, yellow and blue), the stat tiles are flat, and the purple gradient of the menu header is gone: a server without a banner shows a flat panel. The newest tabs of the menu (New and Beta) have tiny dots on them that twinkle. On Migrate, the two message boxes start at the same height. The footer keeps the main links only, and the first two sections of the menu start open.

entries.title: Counting, live counters, image-only and link-only channels are slash commands of their own
entries.summary: They were hidden inside /specialchannels (/specialchannels counting setup). Now each one is in the / menu by its own name: /counting, /counter, /imageonly and /linkonly, with the same subcommands and options as before (for example /counting setup channel:#counting). /specialchannels is not in the menu any more, but the prefix still works exactly as it did: !counting, !counter, !imgonly, !urlonly, !specialchannels counting setup and the short words like !scs.

entries.title: A carousel with the biggest servers that use Petto
entries.summary: The home page has a new carousel with the servers that use Petto and have 500 members or more: up to 15 of them, the biggest first, in two rows that never stop. Each one shows its picture (animated when it is), its name, the badge the Discord app shows next to it (partnered, verified, discoverable, community or its boost level), the members online and the members in all. When a bigger server shows up, it takes the place of the last one. A server that does not want to be here can turn off Show this server in the public ranking in its General settings in the dashboard.

entries.title: The numbers of Petto in the support server
entries.summary: The support server has a new category called @ stats with two voice channels that everybody can see and nobody can join: one with the members of all the servers that use Petto and one with the number of servers, as whole numbers (12,480, not 12K). Petto updates them every 10 minutes.

entries.title: A new home page in ash grey, with the dashboard on a laptop and on phones
entries.area: Web › Home, Features, Premium and Commands
entries.summary: The home page was rebuilt. Under the title there is a laptop with the real dashboard, then three phones in a fan to show that everything can be set up from a phone, three small animated drawings for the protections (anti-nuke, anti-raid and AutoMod) and Discord windows on a laptop and a phone. The home, Features, Premium and Commands now use a cooler ash grey with a silver accent instead of the peach (the light theme and the dashboard are the same). The animations stop when your device asks for less motion.

entries.title: Home fixes, more animated drawings and pictures that open when you tap them
entries.area: Web › Home, Features, Premium and Commands
entries.summary: The phones of the home page now fit the screen without being cut, and a tap on a side phone brings it to the middle (a tap on the middle one opens it bigger). The Discord windows inside the laptop and the phone are drawn at the scale of a real screen, and the laptop no longer touches the announcement. Features, Premium and Commands have a new animated isometric drawing each: the bot and its modules, the plans of 1, 3 and 5 servers, and a keyboard. Any Discord picture of the site opens bigger when you tap it, and closes with a tap outside, the X or Escape.

entries.title: /247: Petto stays in a voice channel for good, with a status
entries.summary: New command `/247` (or `!247`): pick a voice channel with `/247 set` and Petto joins it, muted and with the sound off, and stays there for good: it comes back by itself after a restart, and if somebody moves or kicks it. It writes a status on the channel ("Watching the server 24/7" in the language of the server, or the text you choose; `/247 status` changes it). `/247 info` shows where it is and `/247 off` makes it leave. If music is playing in the server it waits and comes back when it ends. Petto needs View Channel and Connect in the channel, and Set Voice Channel Status to write the status.

entries.title: Stay in voice in the dashboard
entries.summary: New page "Stay in voice" (Community): turn it on or off, pick the voice channel, write the status of the channel and choose whether Petto joins with the sound off. It saves with one button and Petto does it within a minute. It is also in the list of modules, the side menu (with the green dot when it is on) and the finder.

entries.title: Add Petto to your own account: /action, /avatar, /banner, /userinfo and /birthday anywhere
entries.summary: People can now add Petto to their account ("Add to my apps") and use five commands in any server, in direct messages and in group chats, even where Petto is not a member: `/action` (hugs, pats and more, without the counters and the answer button there), `/avatar`, `/banner`, `/userinfo` (the account, without the part of the server) and `/birthday` (`set`, `view` and `remove` keep a personal birthday that only you can see). `/avatar`, `/banner`, `/userinfo` and `/birthday` are slash commands of their own now. Every other command stays only for servers. To make room, `/clearinvites`, `/pauseinvites`, `/stripstaff` and `/giveawaypreset` are registered in each server; they work the same.

entries.title: Home: no more small labels, a shorter animated title and phones that do not cover the pictures
entries.summary: After a review of the home page: the small label above the titles is gone, the long title of the phones section is now one line that changes by itself ("Everything you can set up," and then "you can set up from your phone") so it takes less space and still says the same, and the phones show a thin bar at the top, so the notch and the rounded corners no longer cover the top of the pictures. The fan of phones also leans less and sits a little to the right, so it does not go over the text.

entries.title: The phones of the home look like a real phone that somebody is using
entries.summary: The phones now have a status bar (time, notch, signal, wifi and battery), the line of gestures at the bottom, and a finger that touches the screen now and then, one phone after the other. The picture is shown whole between the two bars, so nothing is covered, and the Discord phone has the same look.

entries.title: The commands page opens much faster
entries.summary: The page of commands had every one of the 1,500 commands drawn at once (48,000 elements, 4.5 MB), so it was slow to open, above all on a phone. Now only the first category is drawn; the rest are put in when you open them, search or follow a link, and the example and the other ways to type a command are made when you open its row. It has about 5,700 elements and 2.6 MB: it is ready in about 0.35 s on a computer (it was 1.8 s) and 1.6 s on a slow phone (it was 8.5 s). Search, the slash and prefix switch, the counts and the links to a command work the same.

entries.title: An isometric drawing while your profile loads
entries.summary: When you go to your profile from any page of the site, a curtain with an isometric drawing (three blocks that go up and down) shows while it loads, and the profile comes in softly instead of just appearing. The same drawing replaces the spinning rings in the other loading curtain of the dashboard.

entries.title: Public pages: no small labels, numbers with title and subtitle, everything centered
entries.area: Web › Home, Features, Premium, Commands and Stats
entries.summary: The small label above the titles is gone on every public page (one rule for all of them), the buttons under a section are centered, and the numbers of the home and of the Stats page have a title, a subtitle for each figure and the same width as the rest of the page. The head of the Stats page is centered like the others.

entries.title: Statistics charts: move a window over the days and the numbers follow
entries.area: Web › Stats page, dashboard statistics and Home
entries.summary: Under the charts of days there is now a small strip with a window. Drag it to slide over the days, pull its edges to make it longer or shorter, or tap the strip to jump: the rest of the chart is shaded and the total, the average per day and the change against the period before count up and down as you move. It works with a finger and with the arrow keys, and 'Whole range' brings everything back. It is in the public Stats page, in every server's statistics and in a sample chart on the Home. Charts also wait until you can see them to draw their line and grow their bars.

entries.title: Features, Premium and Commands no longer look zoomed out and cut on a phone
entries.area: Web › Features, Premium, Commands and Home on phones
entries.summary: On a phone the Features page first looked too big and then seemed cut at the right side, with the bottom bar going off the screen. The faint grid drawn behind the isometric picture went outside the page and made it wider than the screen, so the phone zoomed everything out to fit it. Nothing that is drawn outside the page can do that now, on every public page. Tried at 360, 390 and 412 px wide.

entries.title: /247 from the dashboard: Petto joins the voice channel within 20 seconds
entries.summary: When the 24/7 switch was turned on in the dashboard, Petto could stay out of the voice channel: the job that puts it in looked once a minute and was paused when the bot was under load. It now looks every 20 seconds, is never paused, and the log says each time why Petto is not in a channel (for example, it lacks Connect). Remember that Petto needs View Channel and Connect in that channel.

entries.title: Dashboard menu: the Petto banner is back for servers without a banner
entries.summary: A server that has no banner of its own shows the Petto picture at the top of the side menu again. It had been removed by mistake together with the purple gradient behind it; the gradient stays gone, the picture is back.

entries.title: Statistics charts: a smoother window, steady numbers and no bright tip at the start of the line
entries.area: Web › Stats page, dashboard statistics and Home
entries.summary: The window under the charts now glides with your finger or mouse instead of jumping day by day, and the numbers follow it a moment behind. The percentage of a change (members and servers) always stays on its own line under the number, so it no longer jumps up and down. The shade over the days outside the window now covers the start of the line, which used to show a bright tip on the left.

entries.title: Verification by letters: the form is answered at once, so a busy bot no longer fails it
entries.summary: When the bot was slow, a member who typed the right letters could be verified and still get no answer, and the staff log showed "Unknown interaction" errors. Discord only waits three seconds for the form, and the bot used to look up the member, run the checks and give the roles first. Now it answers the form first and does the rest afterwards, so the member always sees the result. A form that still arrives too late changes nothing and the member just tries again.

entries.title: New page: the history of Petto
entries.area: Web › Petto History (Community menu and footer)
entries.summary: There is a new page that tells where Petto comes from, in English, Spanish and Portuguese, in the first person of the person who leads Petto: the brand and the team began on September 18, 2017, the bot you add today was created on April 19, 2026 and this website in August 2026. It goes year by year (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026), with its hard years told as they were, and answers why the site says 2017. You find it in the Community menu and in the footer.

entries.title: A page that was not found is no longer kept by the browser
entries.summary: After a new version of the site was published, someone who opened a new page a moment too early (for example the Spanish version of a page that had just been added) kept the "404 page not found" on their phone for hours, even when the page already existed. Now a page that was not found is never kept, so the next visit shows the page as soon as it is there.

entries.title: /embed create no longer breaks with a very long name
entries.summary: Creating an embed with a very long name (about 60 characters or more) failed with an "Invalid string length" error, and the embed was saved without its editor, so it could not be opened. Now a name can have 50 characters at most: Discord stops it while you type, and Petto says the limit in your language if it still comes in, before saving anything. An embed that was saved before with a longer name tells you to delete it and create it again with a shorter one.

entries.title: New: the user content policy and how to ask for your data to be deleted
entries.area: Web › Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
entries.summary: The Terms now have a section for content people upload to their own profile (backgrounds, GIFs, badges): what you upload is your choice and your responsibility, every image and every frame of a GIF is reviewed for content that is not allowed, and the email linked to your Discord is kept as a contact for copyright claims. The Privacy Policy now has a section to ask for what is registered about you to be deleted: ordinary data within 0 to 90 days, sensitive data (emails, real names, passwords) within 0 to 30 days, and a card number entered by mistake within 0 to 3 days. Both follow Colombian, Canadian and European (GDPR) rules, in English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: New: your profile is a picture, with badges you can show
entries.summary: /profile and !profile now answer with a picture: your avatar and banner, your name, your level, rank, messages and voice time (with its unit) in the server, and a showcase of badges. The showcase has six hexagons: you have one place for free, and the plans open more (2 with Bronze, 4 with Silver, 6 with Gold), each with its star next to your name. You can also turn on the badges of the Fablo pack (Furro, Boykisser, Hetero and Femboy, free for everybody) with /profile badge and choose their order with /profile showcase. The old card with your rating, uploads, requests and partnerships is now /profile server.

entries.title: New: ceramos, a daily reward, and a shop of badges with frames
entries.summary: Ceramos are the new currency of your profile. /daily gives you some every day (2 with no plan, 5, 10 or 20 with Bronze, Silver or Gold) and /ceramos shows your wallet. In /ceramos shop you can buy badges of countries and languages for 20 ceramos each: you keep them for good, no daily cost. With /ceramos upgrade you can give a badge a better frame, bright (15) or divine (40), that shows in your profile picture. Choose which of your badges to show with /profile showcase.

entries.title: New: the Badges page, with every country flag, to buy and show your badges
entries.summary: Your account now has a Badges page (petto.sbs/dash/badges). It has the showcase of your profile picture and a shop with 253 countries, each with its real flag, languages and the free Fablo pack. Look for a badge by tab or by name, filter by the ones you own, and click one to buy it with ceramos, give it a better frame (bright or divine), turn a free one on or off, or put it in or take it out of your showcase. You can also claim your daily ceramos there. It works on a phone too.

entries.title: New: seasonal and special badges, made by hand, with a limited sale
entries.summary: The team can now make badges of its own: with a picture, a name in three languages, a price (free or paid), the days of the sale, a plan that is needed, or a rule that gives it by itself (a voter, a booster). A Christmas badge, for example, can be on sale from today until January 1: whoever buys it keeps it for good and can wear it whenever they want, and whoever does not can never get it again. These badges have their own Special tab in your Badges page, with the end of the sale shown.

entries.title: New in the wiki: profile picture, badges and ceramos
entries.summary: The wiki has two new pages, in English, Spanish and Portuguese: Profile picture and badges (the picture of /profile, the showcase by plan and how to choose what you wear) and Ceramos and the badge shop (/daily, /ceramos, prices, frames, seasonal badges and the Badges page of the dashboard), both with screenshots. Reviews and profiles now says that the card with the numbers of the server is /profile server, and the changelog has the entry of the day.

entries.title: New: banners, name fonts and packs in the shop, and every badge can be edited
entries.area: Bot + Web › Shop of the profile
entries.summary: Your profile picture can now have a banner and a name font that you buy with ceramos and keep for good: look at the new Customize name and Customize profile pages in your account, or use /ceramos shop (banners, name fonts, packs), /ceramos buy, /profile banner and /profile font. The shop starts with 24 name fonts, like Press Start 2P, Monoton, Cinzel or Lobster. Packs group badges, banners or fonts: free, for a plan, for some days only, or sold whole for less than the pieces. The team can edit any badge, even the countries and the Fablo pack, with a new Shop editor.

entries.title: Your banner on your rank card, and no ring around the avatar
entries.summary: The default rank card (/levels rank) now shows the banner you put on from the shop, darkened a little so the numbers stay easy to read; a server that designed its own rank card keeps its design. Banners are cut to the same size (1024 x 320) when they are uploaded, so they look right on your profile picture, in the shop and on the rank card. The default rank and welcome cards also lose the ring around the avatar. In packs you can now buy the whole pack or one piece at a time.

entries.title: New: plans, My plan, daily reward and ceramos movements, in a new menu
entries.summary: Your account menu is now grouped: Main (Overview, Daily reward), Subscriptions (Plans, My plan, Premium), Personalization (Badges, Customize name, Customize profile), Ceramos (Movements) and Account. The Plans page shows Bronze, Silver and Gold with the ceramos a day and the places in the showcase that each one already gives; the rest of what they will give is marked Soon. My plan shows your plan and when it ends, Daily reward lets you claim your ceramos, and Ceramos movements lists your last 50 movements. Payments are not connected yet: for now the team gives the plans by hand from a new User plans page.

entries.title: Plans can now be bought and cancelled from the website
entries.summary: On the Plans page you can now choose Bronze, Silver or Gold and pay with Polar; your plan is switched on as soon as the payment arrives, renews by itself and ends by itself if you cancel. My plan has a Payments and cancel button that opens your Polar portal. Before paying, the page shows the refund and cancellation rules and asks you to accept them. Premium pages also say, with the same two rules, that Premium is a paid feature. The preview of Customize name and Customize profile now falls back to your Discord banner.

entries.title: New: design your own rank card, with 21 backgrounds in the shop
entries.summary: There is a new page, Rank card, in your account menu. Pick a background (15 free game backgrounds, 6 landscapes that cost ceramos, the designs of Petto or your profile banner), the color of the bar, the font, the color of the text, the theme and the layout, and see your card change live. It is the card every server shows for you when it has not designed its own. Everything is free except a bar with two colors, which costs 40 ceramos once. The backgrounds are also in Customize profile, each with its credit.

entries.title: /rank now has a button to customize your rank card
entries.summary: Under your own rank, /rank and !rank now show a button, Customize your rank, that opens the new Rank card page of the website, where you choose your background, bar colors, font and layout. It appears in the language of the server and it is not shown under somebody else's rank.

entries.title: Name fonts from the shop now show at full size on /profile
entries.summary: If you had put on a name font from the shop, your name came out tiny on the /profile picture, in the normal font, instead of in the font you bought. Now the name is drawn big in your font. The buy window of Customize name also stops showing a green button when you do not have enough ceramos: it is grey now.

entries.title: Your banner now fills the whole profile picture, and the shop has 7 packs
entries.summary: The /profile picture now shows your banner behind everything (avatar, numbers and badges), a little darker toward the bottom so it stays easy to read, instead of a strip on top with a dark band under it. The preview in Customize name and Customize profile is the same card. The shop starts with 5 packs of banners (GTA VI, Forza Minecraft and Halo, Sanrio and Call of Duty are free; Cities and landscapes costs 800 instead of 1150) and 2 packs of name fonts (Retro and arcade for 700, Elegant letters for 400). Free packs can be taken whole with one click.

entries.title: A notice about ceramos: new ways to get them are coming
entries.summary: Wherever you see your ceramos (Daily reward, Ceramos movements, Badges, Customize name, Customize profile and Rank card) there is now a notice: ceramos are scarce for now and come mostly with a paid plan, and we are working on new ways to get them. A new way to earn them is on its way.

entries.title: The profile preview no longer overlaps and shows more of your banner
entries.summary: In Customize name and Customize profile, on a phone the numbers (level, rank, messages, voice) used to cover the badges in the preview. The preview is now taller, lays things out one under the other so nothing overlaps, shows the numbers in two rows on narrow screens, and zooms in on your banner so more of it is seen.

entries.title: Customize pages, Daily reward and My plan fill the page; the Petto background shows with no banner
entries.summary: Customize name and Customize profile now have the preview and the packs on the left (the packs show a few of their pieces) and the search and the pieces on the right, so no corner is left empty. When you have no banner, the preview (and your /profile picture) shows the Petto background, the one the menu shows. Daily reward now has three cards (your ceramos, the ceramos a day of each plan and your latest movements) and My plan lists what your plan gives, instead of one small card in a corner.

entries.title: Buy ceramos: four packs, from 500 to 2,000 ceramos
entries.summary: You can now buy ceramos whenever you want, besides getting them with a plan or the daily reward. Pile of coins: 500 ceramos for $2.99. Small bag: 850 for $4.99. Big bag: 1,200 for $7.99. Treasure chest: 2,000 for $11.99. They are in the new page Buy ceramos of the menu, you pay in Polar, and the ceramos arrive a few seconds after the payment and never expire. Use them for banners, name fonts, packs and badges. A pack shows as not available until its payment product is set up.

entries.title: Economy: a preview of the four coins and the economy of a server
entries.summary: The server dashboard has a new zone, Economy, marked Soon. It is a preview, nothing works or is saved yet: the four coins of the global economy (bronze, silver, gold and mithril), how they change (200 bronze for 1 silver, 100 silver for 1 gold, 50 gold for 1 mithril, 100 mithril for 1 ceramo), a switch to use the global economy in a server, and the economy of your own server. With the global economy a person keeps their coins and streaks everywhere, and coins can become ceramos, so ceramos can also be earned and not only bought.

entries.title: Wiki: a User section under the language selector, and the verification page fixed
entries.summary: The wiki has a new selector under the language one: Server and User. In User you find your profile picture, customizing your name and profile, your rank card, ceramos, buying ceramos, plans and a preview of the economy, in English, Spanish and Portuguese, with pictures. The Verification page no longer calls it an entry filter, and now says that the email code is an optional extra inside Verification, not a separate system.

entries.title: /ceramos top: the ten people with the most ceramos
entries.summary: The new command /ceramos top shows the ten people with the most ceramos, with a medal for the first three. Only their names are shown and nobody is pinged. Also, the packs of ceramos that are bought now show as Pack of ceramos bought in your movements, instead of a raw word.

entries.title: The team can give ceramos from the dashboard, with limits the owner sets
entries.summary: There is a new staff page, Give ceramos. The owner and the people the owner lists give ceramos to a person with a note, and the gift shows in their movements as a gift from the team. The owner sets how much can be given in one gift and how much each person of the team can give in a day, can switch it off for the team, and chooses who is on the list. The owner has no daily limit. It is not available to anyone else.

entries.title: A read-only API: read your ceramos, plan and movements with a key
entries.summary: There is a new page, API keys, in your account menu. Make up to three keys and use them to read your ceramos, your plan and your last 50 movements from your own programs. A key can only read, only sees your own data, is shown once and allows 60 reads a minute. The packs of ceramos can also be read without a key. The wiki has a new page, API keys and the read-only API, with the endpoints, an example and the errors.
